findings.issue: Missing Axis 1 (provenance) label. The book's stated convention (Preface, book p. xi) requires every load-bearing quantitative claim to carry 'Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED])'. This MLA reduction calculation is derived from DeepSeek first-party model geometry (n_h=128, d_h=128, d_c=512, d_h^R=64) but carries only Axis 2 [DERIVED] with no Axis 1 provenance tag (should be [1P][DERIVED]).
findings.fix_instruction: Change '[DERIVED]' to '[1P][DERIVED]' in the Bytes/token cell of the Reduced-width per-token row of the §1.1.4 taxonomy table.

findings.evidence: Book p. 8, Fig 1.1 caption: "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; also Fig 1.2 (p. 11): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; Fig 2.1 (p. 16): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; Fig 4.1 (p. 80): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; Fig 5.1 (p. 100/99): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; Fig 6.1 (p. 103): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]"; Fig 8.1 (p. 147): "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]".
findings.issue: Recurrence of label-pair format violation: the Preface (book p. xi) states 'A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes… the two tags are set with no space between them.' Figures labeled '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' provide only Axis 1 ([ILLUSTRATIVE]) with 'conceptual' as descriptive text inside the same bracket — no valid Axis 2 epistemic status ([FACT]/[DERIVED]/[ASSUMPTION]/[HYPOTHESIS]/[UNRESOLVED]) is present. This affects at least 7 figures across Chapters 1–8. By contrast, figures that do carry proper pairs (e.g., Fig 7.5 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', Fig 7.7 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]') follow the convention correctly.
findings.fix_instruction: For each conceptual figure, add a valid Axis 2 label as a separate adjacent tag, e.g. '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] conceptual' — or add an explicit exception in the Preface's label rule stating that purely conceptual figures with no load-bearing quantitative claims may carry Axis 1 alone.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 26 (Ch 1 taxonomy table, MLA row): "MLA ~50–60× less for DeepSeek-class geometry: 2·n_h·d_h = 2×128×128 = 32,768 dims per layer per token for full MHA vs d_c + d_h^R = 512+64 = 576 for MLA, 32,768/576 ≈ 57× [DERIVED]" | PDF p. 60 (Ch 3): "MLA-style latent attention does not stop the growth: it cuts the bytes/token constant (~50–60× for DeepSeek-class geometry [DERIVED])"
findings.issue: A load-bearing quantitative claim (the ~50–60× / ~57× MLA KV-width reduction, which Ch 3 and Ch 7 §7.7 rely on) carries a bare [DERIVED] tag with no Axis-1 provenance, violating the Preface's rule that 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair'. The 'DeepSeek-class geometry' inputs (n_h = 128, d_h = 128, d_c = 512, d_h^R = 64) are also quoted without naming the first-party source they come from. Recurrence check: the same bare-tag pattern recurs at Ch 3 p. 39; sibling rows in the same table carry full pairs, so the two instances are the only bare [DERIVED] tags in the covered chapters.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace the bare [DERIVED] with a full pair — e.g. [1P][DERIVED] naming the DeepSeek MLA paper/model card for the geometry — in both places, and add the geometry's provenance to the Ch 1 table cell (which currently gives only the arithmetic, not the source of n_h, d_h, d_c, d_h^R).
